title: Grape Sorbet
changes_from_base: Raw dark grapes crushed and strained, with a little corn syrup and lemon, replace the mango, lime and cooked syrup.
summary: A deep purple sorbet that tastes like biting into a ripe dark grape, made from just grapes, sugar and a drop of lemon.

ingredients.item: dark grapes, such as Concord, stemmed and rinsed
light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Crush
steps.text: Pulse the grapes in the blender just until they burst and turn to juice, about 10 seconds; do not blend long enough to grind the seeds, which taste bitter.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Push the pulp through the sieve into the jug with a spoon, pressing hard on the skins. You should have about 650 ml of purée.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Whisk in the sugar, corn syrup and salt until the sugar has dissolved, then taste and add lemon a few drops at a time until the grape flavour is bright.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and chill for at least 3 h, until very cold.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn for 20-25 min, then pack into the container and freeze for at least 3 h. Soften for 10 min before scooping.

tips: Concord or other strongly scented dark grapes give the most flavour; seedless red grapes work too.
Pulse only briefly so the seeds stay whole and do not add bitterness.
Serve with a few frozen grapes on the side.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer for up to 1 week; sorbet turns icy after that. Soften for 10 min before scooping.
